messages:
Ivy L: FYI — Acme reported a sudden p99 spike for inference requests from APAC region ~09:40 UTC, observed by their SRE. They see 200–400ms extra tail latency. Trace they sent: https://traces.redwood.ai/trc_0a1b2c (attached).
InfraBot: alert: customer.p99_latency.ap-southeast spike 2026-03-17T09:40:12Z -> 380ms, threshold 200ms. Auto-sample trace trc_0a1b2c.
Raj P: looking. Can people paste the sampled trace here if available? Need to know whether this is client-side or our egress path.
Marta G: pasted the sampled trace output below — short summary: requests from ap-southeast are getting routed through an unexpected us-east egress proxy before hitting model-host in us-east, then back to ap-southeast. That explains the extra ~200ms + cross-region RTT.
Marta G: ```
trace_id: trc_0a1b2c
hops:
  1  client (APAC) -> edge-ap-southeast-1 (INGRESS)    12ms
  2  lb-edge-ap-southeast (cluster)                    3ms
  3  egress-proxy-us-east-1 (egress)                 230ms  <-- unexpected
  4  model-host-us-east-1 (model)                      40ms
  5  egress-proxy-us-east-1 (egress)                  35ms
  6  edge-ap-southeast-1 (return)                     12ms
  total: ~332ms
```
Ivy L: That matches what Acme sees. They said traffic was healthy before 09:35 and then this kicked in after a deploy to routing-config.
Raj P: ok, two quick hypotheses: (1) a routing-config canary mis-tagged the ap region and sent to fallback us-east pool, or (2) envoy/eBPF based egress selector fell back due to capacity. I'll check routing-config commits and pool capacity around 09:30-09:40.
Sam T: I'm seeing a config rollout at 09:33 that modified region-affinity TTL from 10m -> 7d in the canary branch. If affinity cookie got longer, stale sticky entries could have preferred an older us-east mapping.
Marta G: Cross-checking with rollout logs: config/route-affinity v2.7.1 was applied to 10% of edges at 09:32 as a canary. The canary included a fallback bias increase to us-east for 'low-memory' pools. Seems like edges with transient memory pressure chose fallback.
Ivy L: Customer says they saw it after a sudden spike in their concurrent requests. Could be our fallback policy reacting to momentary pool pressure and sending to us-east.
Raj P: Repro notes: I ran a synthetic from ap-southeast with load generator 200 RPS over 2m and observed the same egress flip after queue depth hit threshold. Steps to repro:
- run `wrk -c 100 -t 8 -d 2m https://edge.ap.redwood/api/v1/generate`
- watch `kubectl -n runtime get hpa` and our egress-metrics dashboard
- check trace sampling for trace when the HPA scales down

Marta G: Short-term mitigation: force region override for Acme by setting `X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1` at the edge via per-tenant header injection (support route). This will bypass fallback routing logic for that tenant.
Sam T: I've applied the header injection for tenant `acme-corp` at 09:56 UTC on the support route. Please confirm with Acme.
Ivy L: I messaged Acme: asked them to do a couple of test requests and paste new trace. Waiting...
Ivy L: Acme reply: after the override latency returned to normal, p99 ~55ms. They attached trace trc_0a1b2c-2 which shows no us-east hop.
Marta G: Root cause summary (early): canary rollout changed affinity TTL and fallback bias; under transient memory pressure some edges preferred fallback us-east pools, creating cross-region detours. Two contributing factors: sticky affinity too long + fallback bias tilt.
Raj P: Actions: (1) Roll back canary change that extended affinity TTL (rolled back at 10:05) — done. (2) Publish a temporary guard to prefer local region unless explicit capacity alarm fires (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1123). (3) Add a test in canary to simulate short-term memory pressure and watch routing decisions.
Sam T: I'll add the HPA / pool-pressure simulation to the canary gate. ETA 2 business days.
Marta G: We'll follow up with a post-incident note and add a dashboard alert for cross-region hop count increase (new metric: `router.hops.cross_region.p99`).
Ivy L: Thanks all — passing this back to support ops to close with customer.
InfraBot: ticket updated: support/ACME-482 -> status: mitigated; notes added.
Raj P: Left TODO: schedule root-cause writeup with networking and runtime teams.
Marta G: small note — please include the trace sample logs and the canary commit id (config/route-affinity@f6d2b9) in the writeup.
Ivy L: will do. :thumbsup:
